summary: A template for the optional `.env` file that `iip/config.py` loads at startup with python-dotenv. It documents every setting the app reads, so copying it to `.env` and editing values reconfigures the platform without code changes. The real `.env` is excluded by `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore`, so secrets never reach version control or a container image.

notes.text: Instructions: copy this file to `.env` and never commit the copy. Every setting has a built-in default, so the app also runs with no `.env` at all.
Explains the API key: a shared secret that clients send in the `X-API-Key` header to call write endpoints (POST and PATCH).
The example value. When no key is configured at all, `config.py` falls back to `demo-key-change-me` (the key in the README's curl example), so the two differ; whichever is set here wins.
Explains demo mode: when true, the server injects the key into the dashboard page; when false, the browser asks for it once per session and keeps it in `sessionStorage` (see `web/js/core/api.js`).
Demo mode is on. `config.py` treats `1`, `true`, `yes` and `on` (in any case) as true and anything else as false.
Explains the limiter: a token bucket per client IP address. It guards the write endpoints and the AI analyst endpoint.
240 requests per minute: a full bucket allows a burst of 240, then refills at 4 tokens per second.
The OpenAI key is optional; without it the deterministic analyst answers, so everything works offline.
Left empty on purpose. `config.py` turns an empty value into `None` (`os.getenv(...) or None`), which selects the deterministic analyst.
The chat model requested when a key is set.
Any service that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions API can be used by changing the base URL below.
The API base URL. `config.py` strips any trailing slash, and the analyst posts to `{base}/chat/completions`.
The remaining settings are commented out, so the built-in defaults apply; delete the `#` to override one.

Database location as a SQLAlchemy URL; three slashes mean a path relative to the working directory. Other databases are possible (with their driver installed), because `database.py` only applies its SQLite-specific settings when the URL starts with `sqlite`.
Browser origins allowed to call the API cross-origin (CORS), as a comma-separated list that `_csv` in `config.py` splits.
The network interface to bind. `127.0.0.1` accepts local connections only; the `Dockerfile` sets `0.0.0.0` so the container is reachable.
The port to listen on. It is plain `PORT`, without the `IIP_` prefix, the conventional variable name that many hosting platforms set.
